oracle.identity: In Milo row-vector convention childWorld.v = childLocal.v * parentWorld.m + parentWorld.v, so childWorld - parentWorld == childLocal.v * parentWorld.m EXACTLY. For a pure-rotation parentWorld.m the ratio is identically 1.000. Any ratio != 1 is therefore one of: (a) scale in parentWorld.m, (b) a stale/pinned cached world xfm, (c) wrong parentage.

root_cause.class: native #else branch is NOT alias-safe; the MWCC paired-single asm it replaces IS
root_cause.detail: The native path does `Multiply(a.m, b.m, res.m);` and only THEN computes `res.v = a.v * b.m + b.v`. When the caller passes the destination as the SECOND argument (res === b), the first statement has already overwritten b.m with a.m*b.m, so the translation is computed against the wrong basis. The MWCC __MWERKS__ asm loads all of _a and _b into paired-single registers before any store, so retail is alias-safe. res === a is safe on both paths.
root_cause.observable: BAND_IK_CONS: neutralOffsetLenSq=481.261 (=> neutral hand-to-hip distance 21.94) but |destWorld - targetWorld| = 49.76 for the same constraint -- a 2.27x length blow-up through a Normalize()d (orthonormal) rotation, which is arithmetically impossible unless an input transform was corrupted.
root_cause.primary_aliasing_call_site: BandIKEffector::NeutralWorldXfm (BandIKEffector.cpp:263) `Multiply(tf38, tf, tf)` -- recursive, so the corruption compounds once per bone up the chain. Feeds ApplyConstraints/ApplyPosConstraints -> a bogus IK hand target -> out-of-reach -> ComputeHandPullAndQuat yanks the shoulder -> DoFancyElbow world-pins the detached upperArm.
root_cause.not_affected: Multiply(const Hmx::Matrix3&, const Hmx::Matrix3&, Hmx::Matrix3&) (Rot.cpp:624) builds all nine products as call arguments to out.Set(...), so it is already alias-safe. The Matrix3-aliasing sites in the sweep are therefore benign.
